content.title: About
content.content: Green Enchilada Sauce (item 4502) is a fragrant Mexican sauce made from tomatoes, green chilies, cilantro and lime. It delivers a bright, mildly spicy flavor with fresh herb notes and can be used as a base for casseroles or as a dip.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A traditional Mexican sauce commonly served with corn tortilla dishes.
The green color comes from fresh green chilies and cilantro, without artificial coloring.
Regional variations exist: Yucatán versions add avocado, while Oaxacan recipes use extra lime juice.
Often used in vegetarian meals as a flavorful alternative to meat fillings.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Lime and green chilies provide a high amount of vitamin C, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Cilantro and tomatoes are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The sauce is low‑calorie, making it a good choice for diet‑friendly meals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cilantro and chilies stimulate bile production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: The chilies can cause discomfort for those with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Cilantro allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cilantro.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lime makes the sauce acidic; people with gastritis should consume it in moderation.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Pour the sauce over baked enchiladas, use it as a chicken marinade, add it to tacos, or serve it as a dip for nachos and vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in the refrigerator in a sealed container for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size containers for up to 3 months.
